meta.basis_caveat: M4 found this basis INCOMPLETE: pair (1,3) is a genuine 14th contact with no row here, and dist rows 36/37 are to be replaced by flush sep rows.  Every headline below is scoped to basis v1; part 4 previews the (1,3) delta.

part1_minimal_dead_certificates.upward_closure_argument: B contains B'  =>  retained(B) subset of retained(B')  =>  cone{grad g_m : m in retained(B)} subset of cone{...retained(B')}. So a y with grad g_m . y > 0 for all m in retained(B') and e_s . y < 0 also has grad g_m . y > 0 for all m in retained(B), and lambda >= 0 with A_retained(B)^T lambda = e_s would give 0 > e_s . y = sum lambda_m (grad g_m . y) >= 0.  One certificate per MINIMAL dead set covers its whole up-set.
part1_minimal_dead_certificates.method: [IV] robust Farkas LP over box(z-hat, r): maximise t subject to inf_box grad g_m . y >= t for every retained m and y[33] <= -t, using the mpmath.iv gradient enclosures of the box; y rationalised at denominator 1e12 and every inf re-verified in mpmath.iv at dps 60.  Fully rigorous per (set, radius).

subdivision.note: one single y does not cover box(z-hat, h_W) for this set; the box is TILED by sub-boxes, each carrying its own [IV]-verified rational Farkas direction.  Sound: the sub-boxes cover the box and each leaf certificate is the same rigorous argument on its own cell.

interval_direct.subdivided_repair_note: the naive interval SAT enclosure is dependency-pessimistic (the max-over-4-axes of differences of interval extrema loses correlation).  Bisecting the 6 coordinates of the two squares (64 sub-boxes) repairs it where needed; the value shown is the worst lower bound over those sub-boxes.

part2_gained_menu_empty.lemma: LEMMA (gained menu empty at h_W).  On box(z-hat, 69/32000) no non-contact pair can touch and no new corner-wall contact can form.  Proof 1 (Lipschitz, M1 constants): pair separation is 4.242641-Lipschitz in ||dz||_inf, so travel <= 4.242641 x 0.00215625 = 0.0091482 < 0.024875 = the smallest non-contact pair gap at z-hat; corner-wall clearance is 3.121320-Lipschitz, travel <= 0.0067303 < 0.548642.  Proof 2 ([IV], independent): the mpmath.iv enclosure of every one of the 41 non-contact pair separations and every one of the 156 non-contact corner-wall clearances over the whole box has a STRICTLY POSITIVE lower bound (worst -0.001067 and 0.542811).  Hence the gained-contact menu of T0.1(ii) is EMPTY on the box and the cone-death certificates of Part 1 need beat only the retained geometric rows.

part3_generation_check.note: EXACT combinatorics: a break set is cone-alive iff it is a subset of the 10-row family that contains none of the 6 forbidden pairs.  Independent sets of the 4-component forbidden graph: 3 x 5 x 5 x 3 = 225 including the empty set, i.e. 224 non-empty.  The M1 JSON list has 224 entries; the M1 report text says 223 -- an off-by-one in the prose, the data are right.

part4_v2_preview_pair_1_3.caveat: This is a PREVIEW, not the v2 result.  It answers only: do the v1 minimal-dead-set certificates still kill once the missing (1,3) contact rows are allowed into the cone?  The v2 basis also replaces dist rows 36/37 by flush sep rows, which changes the minimal-dead-set LIST itself; that awaits m1b_strata.json.

HEADLINE.statement: ON THE A22 38-ROW BASIS v1: every cone-dead break set (all 2^38 - 224 of them) is certified FJ-free in the lambda_0 > 0 branch on box(z-hat, h_W) by one of 34 [IV]-verified rational Farkas directions (33 with a single y, 1 by a subdivided cover), and the gained-contact menu is certified EMPTY on that box, so no gained row can re-feed the cone there.
